sentences.text: To lay a course, draw a straight line from your departure point to your destination, checking that it doesn’t cross land or shoals.
Walk the parallel rulers to the nearest rose and read the true course on the outer ring.
Measure the length of the line with dividers on the latitude scale.
For a leg longer than your dividers can span, set them to a round number like one or five miles and step along the line, then measure the leftover piece.
Label the line, and write your estimated time of arrival at the destination.
